subject: Private offer: harmonize usage floor across clouds + partner retainer split
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudsys.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumenTech Partner <partners@lumentech.com>, legal@cloudsys.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Private offer question — usage floor harmonization + partner retainer split

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to an internal approval but need clarity on two items before procurement signs off: 

1) We plan to accept a private offer that covers both Azure and GCP SKUs. Procurement is asking for a single consolidated "usage floor" that applies across clouds (so metered usage on either cloud counts toward the same commit threshold). Is Redwood able to present a private-offer term that enforces a cross-cloud usage floor? If so, please call out any billing or invoice implications.

2) Our partner LumenTech will take an implementation retainer (one-time) and ongoing channel margin. We need to understand how you typically allocate a fixed retainer against private-offer credits (does it reduce list price or get treated as a separate pass-through?), and what channel margin you can commit to for a multi-region deployment (EMEA-heavy).

If you can share a short example split (list price, passback to partner, net to Redwood) and a term-sheet stub we can circulate with legal, that would be ideal.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our EMEA procurement review is scheduled for Friday.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, CloudSys
procurement@cloudsys.com

--
Attachment: requirements_overview.pdf (stated)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 14:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private offer question — usage floor harmonization + partner retainer split

Marta,

Thanks — great questions. Short answers up front, then a proposed structure.

- Yes: we can structure a private offer that treats Azure + GCP usage as a combined commit for the purposes of a usage floor. That is implemented at the private-offer level (SKU families mapped to a single commitment).
- Billing: invoices will still be issued per-cloud (Azure invoice, GCP invoice) but credits and true-ups are reconciled against a single commit ledger; we'll include a reconciliation appendix in the term sheet.
- Partner retainer: we typically treat an implementation retainer as a pass-through line item (one-time invoice to you, routed to the partner) rather than reducing list price. Ongoing channel margin is applied as a percent of net revenue recognized for the SKUs they resell.

Proposed example (simple):
- List price (combined): $500k/year commit (counts cross-cloud)
- Implementation retainer: $50k (one-time) — pass-through to LumenTech on invoice 1
- Gross discount to CloudSys: 20% off list (net invoice to CloudSys: $400k + retainer)
- Channel margin to LumenTech: 12% of net recognized revenue (annual true-up)
- Redwood net: revenue after discount and channel margin.

Attached: draft term sheet + passback matrix for how the partner retainer and channel margin will flow. Ben / Sergio, can you confirm we can commit to 12% for EMEA and confirm any tax/withholding implications on the pass-through retainer?

Next steps: if CloudSys confirms this structure we will: (1) provision a private-offer template reflecting cross-cloud commit, (2) circulate a term sheet for legal, (3) provide DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Sales — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: Azure_PO_term_sheet_v1.pdf, gcp-azure-passback_matrix.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private offer question — usage floor harmonization + partner retainer split

Kim / Sergio,

Quick internal note: 12% channel margin in EMEA is acceptable on the commit-level SKUs but we should protect Redwood with a clawback on over-refunds/chargebacks (standard 180-day true-up). Also call out VAT handling in the term sheet: if LumenTech invoices the retainer and there's VAT, we need a clause that clarifies whether CloudSys or LumenTech will own that VAT liability — default to partner unless CloudSys requests otherwise.

Proposal tweaks:
- Channel margin: 12% for first 12 months, then review at renewal; 14% cap if partner delivers deployment milestones and increases usage by >25% YoY.
- Retainer: route as pass-through; Redwood to include a labeled line item on the first invoice and mark as partner billable (no discount applied).
- Billing reconciliation: Redwood to provide quarterly reconciliation reports that map Azure and GCP invoices to the combined commit ledger.

Sergio — anything from deal ops / tax we should flag before we send back to CloudSys?

Cheers,
Ben
Head of Channel Sales, Redwood Inference
--
On Tue, 11 Aug 2026 at 14:28, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marta,
> 
> Thanks — great questions...

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudsys.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private offer question — usage floor harmonization + partner retainer split

Hi Marta / CloudSys team,

Appreciate the clear scope. We can proceed with the structure Kimberly proposed with the following clarifications to reduce operational friction: 

1) Cross-cloud commit mechanics: Redwood will publish a quarterly reconciliation (CSV) that maps Azure and GCP usage to the combined commit. This CSV will be referenced in the term sheet appendix and used for true-ups.

2) Partner retainer handling: LumenTech will invoice CloudSys directly for the $50k retainer; CloudSys will pay LumenTech and we will not net the retainer against Redwood invoices. The retainer will be referenced in the passback_matrix for transparency.

3) Channel margin schedule: Confirmed 12% for months 1–12. We will include a milestone-based uplift clause: +2% at renewal if LumenTech achieves the agreed migration milestones (detailed in appendix).

4) Tax & VAT: CloudSys legal to confirm, but our preferred default is partner-liable for VAT on the retainer. Redwood will report gross invoice amounts and deduct channel margin at settlement; any withholding tax should be documented in the passback matrix so we can handle localized reporting.

I've uploaded an updated pricing_summary_v2.xlsx and the finalized passback matrix to the Drive link Kimberly shared and created a short DocuSign envelope that includes the private-offer term sheet.

Action items: 
- Marta: confirm partner VAT stance and whether CloudSys prefers Redwood to route the retainer (if so, we'll change wording).
- CloudSys legal: review term sheet appendix for reconciliation language.
- Kimberly / Ben: once CloudSys confirms, send DocuSign link and target signature by EOD Monday for provisioning before the EMEA rollout.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Deal Operations, Redwood Inference

--
